newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu wants to meet Arafat urgently.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu wants to meet Arafat urgently.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has asked Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for a meeting as soon as possible because of clashes that have killed more than 50 people, an Israeli official said.
A senior official told reporters on Netanyahu's plane returning to Israel from a European trip cut short by the violence that Netanyahu had made the request in a phone call to Arafat from the plane.
Netanyahu returned several hours earlier than planned.

"Netanyahu told him they had to meet this evening as soon as possible because it is very important they speak not by remote control but directly and that they look each other in the eye so that each knows what the other's intentions are," said the official who declined to be identified.
"Arafat didn't say yes, he didn't say no. It is possible they are trying to carry on (with anti-Israeli protests) into Friday for the prayers."
The official quoted Arafat as telling Netanyahu: "I am in control 80 percent."

The official said Netanyahu responded: "That's not enough. You must control much more and foremost you must understand there will be no political gains. You must make a supreme effort and we will also make a supreme effort to bring about disengagement and calm things down."

The official said Netanyahu wanted to bring about "calm and disengagement and afterwards resumption of the diplomatic process." Netanyahu also called U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher but the conversation was cut off, the official said.
The senior official said Israel's main aims at this point were "protecting our forces, disengagement, calming things down on the ground and meeting with Arafat."
The official said that if the Palestinians tried to avoid a meeting, "the indication is clear -- they are continuing to play with fire, but we will see."
Netanyahu's office said the Israeli leader planned to convene his security cabinet later on Thursday.
Palestinian medical officials said 44 Palestinians had died in the West Bank and Gaza clashes and Israel Radio said 11 Israelis had been killed.
